subtitle: Phase Dispersion
tagline: All-pass phase dispersion that stretches a sharp transient into a heavier, frequency-dependent sweep, with a built-in frequency LFO for motion.

body.lead: TB Disperser delays different frequencies by different amounts. A drum hit or synth attack, which normally arrives all at once, is spread into a short sweep, the familiar laser-like zap of phase dispersion.

body.p: Because it changes when frequencies arrive rather than how loud they are, TB Disperser can make drums, bass, and synth attacks feel longer, heavier, and more animated without adding distortion. A dedicated LFO moves the dispersion frequency for motion without automation.

ul: Chain of all-pass sections whose group delay is concentrated around a chosen frequency
AMOUNT, FREQUENCY, PINCH, and SPEED to shape the length and focus of the sweep
Frequency LFO with five shapes, a range of up to ±4 octaves, and a free-running rate
Live display of the group delay across the spectrum, with a readout at the current LFO frequency
Ten factory presets with descriptions, plus user presets, undo, and redo

steps: Centre and delay from FREQUENCY, PINCH, SPEED

note.title: About this manual
text: This manual describes TB Disperser 1.3.0 for Windows (VST3). The current macOS build is version 0.1.2 and may differ from the descriptions here.

ol: Insert TB Disperser on a drum, bass, or synth track. The defaults are `AMOUNT` 70%, `FREQUENCY` 200 Hz, `PINCH` 0%, `+ SPEED` 2.0x, with the LFO off.
Play the material and move `FREQUENCY` {{5}} to the area where you want the sweep: low values for weight, higher values for a brighter zap.
Raise `AMOUNT` {{4}} for a stronger, longer dispersion.
Lower `+ SPEED` {{7}} to stretch the zap into a longer, slower sweep.
Raise `PINCH` {{6}} to concentrate the ringing around FREQUENCY.
For motion, choose an LFO `TYPE` {{8}} and set `RANGE` and `RATE`.

rows: Sets the amount of accumulated phase dispersion by setting how many all-pass sections are active. Higher values give a stronger, longer sweep.
Sets the frequency where group delay is concentrated. Low settings add weight; high settings give a bright, metallic zap.
Concentrates ringing around the selected frequency. At 0% the sections spread over up to ±2 octaves; at 100% they converge into a narrow, ringing focus.
Sets the dispersion speed. Lower values create a longer, slower zap.
Off, Sine, Tri, Saw, Sqr, Rnd · Off
Turns the LFO off or selects one of five shapes. It is a stepped rotary control.
Frequency sweep depth in octaves around FREQUENCY. Zero turns modulation off.
The free-running LFO rate in hertz. It does not follow the host tempo.

note.text: TB Disperser has no dry/wet control. All-pass dispersion changes timing, not level, but if you blend its output with the dry signal on a parallel bus, phase differences can cancel parts of the sound. Check the result in mono.

body.p: LIVE GROUP DELAY plots how long each frequency is delayed (vertical axis, from 0 up to seconds) across the spectrum (horizontal axis, 20 Hz to 20 kHz). The peak of the curve sits around FREQUENCY; AMOUNT raises it, PINCH narrows it, and lower SPEED values stretch it.
With the LFO running, the marker moves with the modulated frequency, and the readout at the top right shows the group delay at that frequency, for example 3.6 ms @ 898.5 Hz.

Use the arrows {{1}} to step through presets (hold to browse quickly), or open the list to choose a Factory or User preset; Space also opens it. Save User Preset stores the current settings under a name of your choice. Undo and Redo step through parameter and preset changes.

body.p: Starting points for common jobs. Adjust them by ear.

recipes.title: Laser snare or clap
recipes.use: A bright, obvious zap on short percussion.
steps: Raise AMOUNT until the zap is clear, then back off so the hit stays tight.

recipes.title: Heavier kick or bass attack
recipes.use: More weight and length without distortion.
steps: Low FREQUENCY settings can sound like a wide phase shift; keep AMOUNT moderate.

recipes.title: Moving synth pad
recipes.use: Slow, evolving phase motion on sustained sounds.
steps: Start with a small RANGE and slow RATE, then widen.

recipes.title: Rhythmic phase pulse
recipes.use: A stepped, rhythmic change of colour.
settings: Set by ear against the groove
steps: RATE is free-running; adjust it until the steps sit with the music.

rows: The low end sounds smeared or hollow.
Lower AMOUNT or raise FREQUENCY. Low frequencies are delayed the most.
Raise AMOUNT, lower + SPEED, or raise PINCH for a more focused ring.
Lower PINCH so the dispersion spreads over a wider range.
Choose a TYPE other than Off and set RANGE above zero.
The LFO is not in time with the song.
RATE is free-running in hertz; adjust it by ear or automate it.
Parts of the sound cancel in mono.
This happens when the dispersed signal is blended with the dry one. Reduce AMOUNT or avoid parallel blending.
